name: Project Aria
summary: Project Aria is Meta's research eyewear platform: sensor-rich glasses with calibrated multi-camera capture, SLAM-grade 6-DoF pose, eye tracking and hand tracking, distributed to academic partners alongside open tooling and datasets. Its significance for manipulation is that it produces metric egocentric data — 3D hand trajectories in a known world frame — rather than raw pixels, and that is what makes a human recording convertible into a robot action target. A second-generation device followed in 2025.
innovation: Calibrated, pose-grounded egocentric capture: hand trajectories arrive in metric 3D rather than needing to be estimated from video afterwards.
Open tooling and data format, which made it the shared substrate for academic human-data robotics.
matters: Turned human video from something you scrape into something you deliberately collect in a geometrically usable form. EgoMimic, EgoZero and much of the 2025 human-data work runs on it.
limits: Limited hardware distribution; captures kinematics but no forces, and hand pose degrades under occlusion.
lineage: The capture instrument that made Ego4D's premise actionable for robot learning.
